subject: Recap: Hosted API volumes & target $/1M — Helios Health

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Subject: Recap: Hosted API volumes & target $/1M — Helios Health

Hi Michelle — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so we can align internal next steps. TL;DR: we captured an initial expected monthly token range and peak TPS shape; please confirm the numbers below so Ben/SE can produce a scoped pricing proposal.

Summary of what you shared
- Primary use: inbound summarization + clinical Q&A for patient support (low hallucination tolerance).
- Expected monthly token volume (initial 6–12 mo): ~90M–150M tokens (working estimate; you mentioned seasonal campaigns could lift this).
- Typical baseline TPS: 1.0–1.5 TPS. Peak TPS during business hours: 6–8 TPS sustained for short windows; brief marketing-triggered spikes up to ~10 TPS for ~5–10 minutes on campaign days.
- Target unit economics: Helios would prefer a fully-burdened target around $35–$45 per 1M tokens (you said $40 as ideal).

Questions / asks for Helios (please confirm):
1) Confirm the working monthly token range above (90M–150M) or give a single-band target you want priced.
2) Confirm whether you need committed slab pricing (1yr) vs month-to-month hosted consumption. If committed, any preferred term (12/24 months).
3) Any procurement constraints we should know up front (PO process, SOC2 evidence, standard MSA redlines)?

Attachments: I attached the traffic snapshot you shared in the call (traffic-snapshot.csv). Ben will follow up with a proposal that includes three pricing scenarios (100M, 150M, 200M committed slabs) and example monthly spend/$/1M math.

Next steps (proposed)
- Ben to send a short pricing scenarios PDF with committed and on-demand comparisons (by EOD tomorrow).
- If numbers look good, Vanessa to share MSA + procurement packet and we schedule a 30-min procurement call with Arjun.

If anything above is off, flag it and we'll adjust before we build the formal quote.

Thanks — talk soon,
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap, this looks right to me. A few clarifications: 
- Confirmed monthly target: for budgeting let's model 100M (conservative) and 180M (growth scenario). The 90–150 band you noted is accurate as an early estimate.
- Peak shape: we typically see 1.5–2.0 TPS average during hours, with 6–8 TPS daily spikes. During marketing pushes the short spike can reach 10 TPS as you noted.
- Target pricing: we will push internally for ~$35/1M tokens but understand market realities — please show us committed tiers that hit $35–$45/1M with 12-month commitment options.
- Procurement: Arjun (cc'd) is our procurement lead — primary requirements: SOC2 Type II, data residency in US, standard PO + 60 day net terms, and a short security questionnaire.

Attached: I am sending our procurement intake (procurement-questionnaire-Helios.xlsx) so you can see the items Arjun will flag.

Can Ben include a simple table in the proposal that shows: monthly tokens | $/1M | monthly $ | annualized $ for the scenarios (100M/150M/180M)? That helps our finance team.

Michelle — looping in a quick technical/price sketch before I build the PDF. Below are realistic scenarios and a note on how to cover the bursts you described.

Short notes on traffic and cost drivers
- Effective tokens billed: summarization + system tokens add ~10–20% to raw user tokens depending on prompt length and system messages — we should model +15% to be safe.
- Caching: prefix caching on the runtime can reduce billed tokens for repeated prompts (likely relevant for templated clinical Q&A). We will model a conservative 8% token saving in the scenarios.

Rough pricing scenarios (examples for discussion)
- On-demand (no commit): $75 / 1M tokens (list example) — this is the upper bound, no SLAs for committed throughput.
- 12-month committed slab, 150M tokens/month: $38 / 1M tokens (applies when slab consumed; includes 20% burst buffer for short spikes).
- 12-month committed slab, 100M tokens/month: $45 / 1M tokens (smaller slab = higher unit).

Example math (150M slab, modeled tokens after +15% overhead and -8% caching savings):
- Nominal tokens: 150,000,000
- +15% overhead = 172,500,000
- -8% caching = 158,700,000 billed tokens (~159M)
- Price at $38 / 1M => ~ $6,034 monthly (~ $72k annual)

On bursts: we recommend a committed slab with a managed burst policy: committed capacity covers sustained throughput; short bursts (up to 20% of slab) are allowed and billed against a transient bucket at the committed rate. For spikes beyond that we route to on-demand at a slightly higher short-term rate (we'll show the blended math).

I'll assemble a neat PDF with three scenarios (100M/150M/180M) and the monthly/annual numbers Michelle requested, plus a line for optional dedicated routing (if you need an SLA-backed throughput with guaranteed concurrency). Expect that PDF attached as "slab-pricing-proposal-v1.pdf" — will send EOD.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
